t.7.65.1: Rāghava heard all of that piteous lament of the brahmin, so filled with sorrow and grief.
t.7.65.2: Sorely afflicted with grief, he summoned his ministers, Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva, and his brothers together with the townsfolk.
t.7.65.3: Then eight twice-born brahmins, together with Vasiṣṭha, were ushered in, and they said to the king, who resembled a god, "May you prosper!"
t.7.65.4: Mārkaṇḍeya, and then Maudgalya, Vāmadeva and Kāśyapa, Kātyāyana, and then Jābāli, Gautama, and likewise Nārada.
t.7.65.5: All these bulls among the twice-born, the ministers and the townsmen as well, have been seated upon their seats, each according to his rank and as is fitting.
t.7.65.7: Having heard those words of the distressed king, Nārada, in the presence of the ṛṣis, replied to the king with auspicious words.
t.7.65.6: To all of them, those men of blazing splendour seated together, Rāghava recounted everything: the reason why the brāhmaṇa was weeping aloud.
t.7.65.8: Hear, O king, how this death of the boy has come to pass at this time; and having heard it, O hero, O Raghunandana, do what must be done.
t.7.65.9: Formerly, O Rāma, in the Kṛta age, only brāhmaṇas were ascetics; at that time, O king, one who was not a brāhmaṇa was in no way an ascetic.
t.7.65.10: In that age, blazing with splendour, become one with Brahman and free from all veils, all who were born then were deathless and far-seeing.
t.7.65.11: Then came the age called Tretā, of men endowed with fine bodies, in which the Kṣatriyas are born endowed with the austerity of the former age.
t.7.65.12: In that age, the Tretā Yuga, those great-souled men were superior in valor and in austerity in their former birth.
t.7.65.13: But all the brahmins and kṣatriyas, both the earlier and the later, who lived in those two ages, were endowed with equal power.
t.7.65.14: But all of them, seeing no greater distinction, then established there the order of the four varṇas everywhere.
t.7.65.15: Adharma, however, set one foot down upon the surface of the earth; and because they were joined with adharma, the twice-born grew feeble.
t.7.65.16: Then, in that former age, the full span of life was made manifest, and people practised only what was auspicious, wholly devoted to truth and dharma.
t.7.65.17: But in the Tretā age, those who lived as brāhmaṇas and as kṣatriya all practised austerities, while the other people rendered service.
t.7.65.19: Then it brought down the second foot of Adharma, and thereupon that age came to bear the name Dvāpara.
t.7.65.18: Then that supreme dharma of theirs passed to the vaiśyas and śūdras, and the śūdras in particular paid honour to all the varṇas.
t.7.65.20: When that age known as Dvāpara was current, in the waning of the yugas, unrighteousness and falsehood grew, O bull among men.
t.7.65.21: In that age known as the Dvāpara, asceticism entered into the Vaiśyas; yet a Śūdra does not attain the dharma of fierce austerity performed, O bull among men.
t.7.65.22: O best of men, one of low varṇa is undergoing very great austerity; for the practice of austerity among those of śūdra birth belongs to the future, to the Kali age.
t.7.65.24: O tiger among kings, whatever evil-minded man commits unrighteousness or a forbidden deed in a king's realm or in his city, he swiftly goes to hell, and so does that king; there is no doubt.
t.7.65.23: The supreme unrighteousness, O Rāma, is that borne by a śūdra in the Dvāpara age. Indeed, O king, at the border of your realm an evil-minded śūdra of great austerity is practicing penance, and because of him this killing of the child has come about.
t.7.65.25: Therefore, O tiger among men, search through your own realm; wherever you see wrongdoing, there make every effort to set it right.
t.7.65.26: Thus, O best of men, there will be an increase of your righteousness, a lengthening of the lifespan of men, and the life of this boy as well.
